messages.content: What are the different properties of Hydrogen?

function.name: look_up_scientific_contributions

message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; 1.00794 u for ^1H) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Molecular form** | Diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions | | **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.44 K) | | **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | | **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 g cm⁻³) | | **Specific heat capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 28.836 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ | | **Heat of vaporization** | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ | | **Reactivity** | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion) and with many metals (forming hydrides). | | **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (hydrogen ion donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺). | | **Isotopes** | • **^1H (protium)** – most abundant (~99.98%)
• **^2H (deuterium)** – stable isotope, ~0.02% natural abundance
• **^3H (tritium)** – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 y | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics. | | **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds (H–H, H–C, H–O, etc.), ionic bonds (as H⁺ or H⁻ in hydrides), and participates in hydrogen bonding (in water, alcohols). | | **Physical state at room temperature** | Gas | | **Solubility in water** | 0.00018 g g⁻¹ (≈0.18 mg mL⁻¹) – very low | | **Flammability limits** | Lower explosive limit (LEL): 4 % (v/v) in air; Upper explosive limit (UEL): 75 % (v/v) | | **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis, petroleum refining), laboratory standard gas, cryogenic coolant, space propulsion, etc. | --- ### Quick Reference Summary - **Atomic number:** 1 - **Molecular form:** H₂ (diatomic) - **Boiling point:** –252.9 °C (20 K) - **Density (STP):** 0.0899 g L⁻¹ - **Ionization energy:** 13.6 eV - **Electronegativity:** 2.20 - **Isotopes:** ^1H (protium), ^2H (deuterium), ^3H (tritium) These properties make hydrogen the lightest element, highly reactive, and a cornerstone of both chemistry and physics.
